Detect v-structures in the constraint-based skeleton

Source: R/cpdag.R
mc_find_vstructures.Rd

Runs the PC skeleton search on the estimated between-response covariance and, for each unshielded triple \((i, k, j)\) (\(i - k - j\) with \(i\) and \(j\) nonadjacent), decides whether \(k\) is a collider \(i \to k \leftarrow j\), under one of three rules. A collider is identified by the absence of \(k\) from the sets that separate \(i\) and \(j\), which is why the search conditions on subsets and not on all other responses at once.

Usage

mc_find_vstructures(
  fit,
  alpha = 0.05,
  max_ord = NULL,
  df_residual = NULL,
  orient_rule = c("standard", "conservative", "majority")
)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

alpha

significance level of the second-order separation test.

max_ord

maximum conditioning order passed to mc_pc_skeleton and to the enumeration of separating sets. A test the skeleton search cannot form is skipped with the warning described there.

df_residual

optional residual degrees of freedom passed to mc_pc_skeleton and to the reported separating-set tests: NULL for the approximation by \(n\), a number, or "auto", which takes \(\nu_e\) from mc_residual_df and refuses a fit for which it is not exact.

orient_rule

"standard" (default), "conservative" or "majority".

Value

A data frame with columns i, k, j, is_collider, applied, ambiguous, n_sets, prop_center, pcor and p_value. The last two refer to the test of \(i\) and \(j\) given the set the skeleton recorded; applied is FALSE for a collider whose orientation was withheld because another collider required the opposite direction on one of its edges. Under "standard" the columns n_sets and prop_center are NA, since no collection is formed.

The three rules

"standard" consults the single set the skeleton recorded for the pair and declares a collider when the center is absent from it. It is the rule of Spirtes, Glymour and Scheines and it depends on which separating set the enumeration happened to reach first. "conservative" enumerates every set that separates the endpoints on the final skeleton and declares a collider only when the center is in none of them, a non-collider when it is in all of them, and leaves the triple ambiguous otherwise (Ramsey, Zhang and Spirtes, 2006). "majority" decides by the proportion of separating sets containing the center, with a tie left ambiguous (Colombo and Maathuis, 2014). Combined with the order-independent skeleton, the last two make the procedure independent of the order of the responses.

References

Spirtes, P., Glymour, C. and Scheines, R. (2000). Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd edition. MIT Press.

Ramsey, J., Zhang, J. and Spirtes, P. (2006). Adjacency-faithfulness and conservative causal inference. Proceedings of the 22nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 401-408.

Colombo, D. and Maathuis, M. H. (2014). Order-independent constraint-based causal structure learning. Journal of Machine Learning Research 15, 3921-3962.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 600
z1 <- rnorm(n); z2 <- rnorm(n); z3 <- 0.7*z1 + 0.7*z2 + rnorm(n)  # collider
d <- data.frame(y1 = z1, y2 = z2, y3 = z3, x = rnorm(n))
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x, y2~x, y3~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_find_vstructures(f)
#>   i k j is_collider applied ambiguous n_sets prop_center       pcor   p_value
#> 1 1 3 2        TRUE    TRUE     FALSE     NA          NA 0.03574128 0.3823036
# }
